Subject: Outage on Oct 2 — request for SLA credit eligibility & numbers

Hi Rishi,

Thanks for the incident write-up you circulated last week. QuantumForge saw a five-hour partial degradation on Oct 2 that affected our inference pipelines (throughput dropped and a subset of requests timed out). Our procurement team is asking for a formal SLA credit eligibility confirmation and the credit calculation so we can reconcile this on our side.

Can you confirm:
- Whether QuantumForge is eligible under our contract (SLA section 4.2)
- The specific hours/minutes of downtime you’re attributing to our account
- The credit amount and method used to calculate it (monthly revenue vs committed spend)

We’d appreciate the numbers and a draft credit note we can attach to our internal ticket. Happy to hop on a quick call if helpful.

Thanks,
Samir
Head of IT Operations
QuantumForge

Samir — thanks for raising this. Short answers up front: yes, QuantumForge is eligible; we’ve calculated the downtime window and a preliminary credit; and we’ll share a draft credit note by Friday.

High-level:
- Incident summary: partial availability degradation from 2026-10-02T01:15:00Z to 2026-10-02T06:20:00Z for the US cluster serving your dedicated capacity.
- Root cause: regression in autoscaling daemon combined with an overloaded prep-cache job (full postmortem linked below).
- Eligibility: per Section 4.2, you meet the threshold for an uptime-based credit.

I’m looping in Finance (Marissa) to confirm the credit calculation method and Support (Evelyn) for the precise per-tenant impact window. I’ve attached the raw uptime logs and a working spreadsheet with the SLO math.

Next steps:
1) Evelyn will confirm the final impacted request-set and exact minutes to be applied.
2) Marissa will confirm whether we apply credit against committed monthly spend or invoice adjustment (per your preference).
3) I’ll send a draft credit note for signature.

Rishi
Director, Customer Success
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Outage on Oct 2 — request for SLA credit eligibility & numbers

Thanks — I reviewed the logs and ran a per-tenant impact extraction. Key points:

- Final impacted window for QuantumForge: 2026-10-02T01:18:00Z to 2026-10-02T05:55:00Z (4h37m). During that window the cluster served at ~48% capacity for your routes; roughly 12% of requests experienced timeouts vs baseline <0.5%.
- We applied the contract SLO rules (exclude scheduled maintenance windows and apply progressive credit tiers).
- Calculation approach used: (downtime minutes / total minutes in month) * committed monthly spend.

Applied numbers (preliminary):
- Month minutes (Oct): 44640
- Affected minutes: 277
- Ratio: 0.62%
- Committed monthly spend on file: $118,000
- Preliminary credit: $118,000 * 0.0062 = $731.60 → round to $732 (we typically round to whole dollars)

Notes and asks:
- Samir, please confirm if you prefer an invoice adjustment or a standalone credit note that posts to your account balance.
- Marissa, please confirm approval path for credits under $2k; policy says manager approval suffices but we often route to finance for tracking.

I can produce a PDF credit note once we have the final preference.

—Evelyn
Senior Support Lead, Redwood Inference
